data.body_html:
Imagine the sun dipping behind La Concha as the strains of a Spanish guitar fill the air. You're on a private boat, gliding out of Puerto Banús, a glass of cava in hand, while a flamenco dancer moves with passion on the deck. This is the tapas flamenco boat cruise in Marbella — an evening that blends the best of the Costa del Sol: the sea, the food, and the soul of Andalusia.

Why a Tapas & Flamenco Cruise is Unforgettable

Marbella is known for its glamour, but the real magic happens on the water. A private charter turns a simple evening into a bespoke experience. You're not just a spectator; you're the host of your own floating fiesta. The combination of live flamenco, Spanish tapas, and the gentle Mediterranean breeze is something you'll talk about for years. Plus, you get the freedom to choose your route, your music, and your pace.

Setting Sail from Puerto Banús

All our cruises depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella's luxury marina. You'll meet your skipper at the dock, board your chosen vessel, and set off along the coast. In the first hour, you can cruise towards the iconic Marbella Marina or the golden sands of the Golden Mile. The skipper will find a calm spot to anchor, where you can enjoy the flamenco performance and tapas while the sun sets over the sea.

Our Fleet for the Perfect Evening

Choose a boat that fits your group size and style. For an intimate dinner for two or a small group, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 guests) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 guests) are ideal. Both are sporty flybridge cruisers with ample deck space. For a larger celebration, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 guests) offers a grand open-plan saloon and a spacious aft deck — perfect for a dance floor. All boats come with a licensed skipper and full safety equipment.

What's Included in Your Charter

Every charter includes a professional skipper, fuel, insurance, and safety equipment. Onboard, you'll find a selection of drinks: water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava. Light snacks are provided, but for the full tapas experience, we add a curated menu of Spanish delicacies — think jamón ibérico, manchego, patatas bravas, and fresh seafood. The flamenco performance (guitarist and dancer) is arranged as an add-on, with a surcharge that we'll quote based on the duration and group size.

Pricing and Booking

For the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39, the price is €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours — all inclusive of skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For larger yachts like the Mangusta 80, the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, which includes a free jet ski. For any other boat in our fleet, pricing is on request via WhatsApp — we'll tailor a package to your needs. To book, simply contact us with your preferred date, group size, and any special requests.

Sample Itinerary: Sunset Cruise

Here's how a typical 3-hour sunset flamenco cruise might unfold:

  • 18:30 — Board at Puerto Banús, welcome drink of cava.
  • 18:45 — Depart, cruise along the coast towards Cabopino.
  • 19:15 — Anchor in a quiet cove (e.g., Cala del Faro).
  • 19:30 — Flamenco guitarist and dancer perform for 45 minutes.
  • 20:15 — Tapas served, enjoy the sunset and open bar.
  • 21:00 — Return to Puerto Banús, drop off.

Private Events and Celebrations

This cruise is perfect for birthdays, anniversaries, proposals, or just a special night out. We can arrange flowers, a custom cake, or a photographer to capture the moments. For corporate groups, it's a memorable way to entertain clients. The flamenco performance can be adapted to be more interactive, perhaps teaching your guests a few steps. Just let us know your vision, and we'll make it happen.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is included in the tapas flamenco boat cruise?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and safety equipment. For the flamenco experience, we add a live guitarist and dancer (surcharge) plus a selection of Spanish tapas. All prices include Spanish IVA (21%).

How much does the tapas flamenco boat cruise cost?

Prices start from €749 for the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 for a 2-hour charter. For longer durations, up to 8 hours, the price is €2,299. The flamenco performance and tapas are an additional cost, which we'll quote based on your group size and menu preferences.

Which boats are available for the flamenco cruise?

You can choose from our fleet at Puerto Banús. Popular options include the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 guests) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 guests) for intimate groups. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 guests) is a stunning choice. Contact us for availability.

What time does the flamenco cruise depart?

We recommend a sunset departure, typically around 18:30–19:30 in summer, to enjoy the golden hour over the Mediterranean. You can also book a daytime slot. All charters depart from Puerto Banús, the iconic marina in Marbella.

Can we customise the tapas menu?

Yes, we can tailor the tapas selection to your preferences, including vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free options. Just let us know in advance. The standard menu includes Spanish classics like patatas bravas, jamón serrano, olives, and manchego cheese.

Is the flamenco performance live?

Absolutely. We arrange a professional flamenco guitarist and dancer to perform live on board. The performance is intimate and interactive, perfect for a memorable evening. The exact configuration depends on the boat size and your group.

What is the cancellation policy?

Cancellations made more than 72 hours before departure receive a full refund. Within 72 hours, a 50% charge applies. If weather conditions prevent sailing, we offer a full refund or reschedule. Contact us for details.

How do I book the tapas flamenco cruise?

Simply send us a WhatsApp message or use the booking form on our website. We'll confirm availability, provide a detailed quote, and answer any questions. Payment is via secure bank transfer or card.
